contexts.text: They exacerbate him () = resistance by falsities... For in proportion as there is resistance there is exacerbation, when there is combat. AE 448:6.
Lest He be angry on account of evils, that is, lest He be exasperated on account of transgressions.
Lest thou exasperate Him () = turning away from Him through falsities from evil; as is evident from the signification of to exasperate or excite anger, when said of the Lord...
If a man were to perceive that he is continually being withdrawn from his delight, he would be exasperated as against one who wanted to murder him. DP 211:2.
When the will is attacked, it exasperates itself in the understanding...
Such is the exasperation of love which is called zeal.
He is then exasperated against truths and goods...
Thus truth and falsity are presented together as if they were conjoined, by which the Angels of Heaven are exacerbated, and turn entirely away.
